wu: Memory Chain: Teacher starts with 'Last week, I visited a market.' Student 1 repeats and adds 'While I was visiting, I bought fruit.' Student 2 repeats and adds 'While they were buying, they met a friend.' Continue around the class.
wuAlt: Photo Prompt: Show a photo of a local Moroccan festival (like Green March). Ask 'What was happening?' Students use past continuous to describe.
Timeline Toss: Write 3 past events on the board. Students toss a ball and make sentences with 'when' or 'while'.
pres: Use 3 flashcards: a wedding, a rainstorm, a power cut. Model: 'I was sleeping when the storm started.' 'We were eating when the lights went out.' Elicit rules for past simple (interrupted actions) and 'when/while'. Check with thumbs-up/down for true/false sentences.
presAlt: Story Chain: Write a 2-sentence story on the board. Students add one sentence with past continuous, then one with past simple to interrupt it.
Realia Show: Bring in a traditional Moroccan tea set. Narrate: 'I was pouring tea when the cup broke.' Students describe their own experiences with objects.
prac: Interrupted Action Chains: In pairs, Student A mimes an action (e.g., cooking). Student B mimes an interruption (e.g., phone rings) and says 'You were cooking when the phone rang.' Swap roles. Teacher circulates to correct tense errors.
pracAlt: While-Clause Game: Give each pair a card with a 'while' clause (e.g., 'While I was walking...'). They must complete it with a past simple action. First pair to shout 'Finished!' gets a point.
Sentence Race: Write 'when' and 'while' on the board. Teams race to write correct sentences using past simple/continuous about local events.
ls: Listen to a 1-minute story about a power cut during Ramadan. Students listen and note 2 'when' moments and 2 'while' moments on a worksheet. Play twice for comprehension.
re: Action Freeze: Teacher calls out an action (e.g., 'praying'). Students mime it. Teacher shouts 'BANG!' and says 'You were praying when the lights went out.' Students freeze and repeat the sentence.
prod: Memory Circle: Each student shares a true memory about a Moroccan holiday (e.g., Eid, Independence Day). They must use one 'when' and one 'while' sentence. Listeners ask follow-up questions.
rw: Read a short story extract about a wedding in Fez. Underline all past continuous verbs with a green pen and past simple with red. Then write 3 sentences about a personal memory using both tenses.
st: Read a short folktale about a clever djinn who interrupts a farmer's work. End with the goodbye routine: 'Today we practiced telling stories about the past using when and while. Thank you for sharing your memories.'
g: Match past simple and continuous cards to make logical sentences (e.g., 'was walking / saw a friend').
Teams race to write sentences on the board using prompts like 'shopping / rain started'.
Student A mimes; Student B interrupts and says a sentence with past simple.
Groups use 3 photos to create a 2-sentence story with past continuous + past simple.
Students toss a ball and make sentences about events on a class timeline.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 50-word story about a Moroccan festival using 3 'while' and 2 'when' sentences.
Support: Use sentence starters like 'I was ______ when ______.' on a worksheet.
hw: Write a paragraph (80 words) about a childhood memory using at least two 'while' sentences.
Record a 1-minute voice message telling a family memory with past simple/continuous.
Find a photo online and write 3 sentences about what was happening when the photo was taken.
tip: Use local context (Moroccan holidays, family gatherings) to make the grammar memorable. Adults connect better to personal stories.
